sentences.text: The name Moanasaurus translates to "Sea Lizard," combining the Māori word for ocean with the Greek term for lizard.
This predator possessed a massive skull reaching 78 cm in length, making it one of the largest members of the Mosasaurinae subfamily.
Fossil remains of this ancient reptile have been unearthed in the North Island of New Zealand.
Taxonomically, the species belongs to the superfamily Mosasauroidea, the family Mosasauridae, and the subfamily Mosasaurinae.
Moanasaurus inhabited the waters surrounding modern-day Japan and New Zealand during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, roughly 70 to 66 million years ago.
Its broader time range extends from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, spanning between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
A PhD thesis proposed that Mosasaurus flemingi is a junior synonym of Moanasaurus mangahouangae, though this classification remains a subject of scholarly discussion.
